correctness.rationale: The focal source supplies the exact kernel factorization \(F_\alpha^{B_A}(z,w)=L_A(z)(1-z\overline w)^{-(\alpha+1)}I\,L_A(w)^*\). Kernel transport gives an isometric multiplication model, so the two identity norms are precisely the multiplier norms of \(L_A\) and \(L_A^{-1}\). For \(\alpha>0\) the vector-valued weighted-area model, and for \(\alpha=0\) the Hardy model, make each multiplier norm equal to the \(H^\infty\) norm. Spectral calculus for \(0\le A\le aI\) gives both norms exactly \(\sqrt{(1+a)/(1-a)}\). The source example has \(a=3/4\), yielding \(\sqrt7\). The proof does not use finite sampling or an unproved computation.

value.rationale: The focal paper's nonrigidity theorem identifies the spaces only up to equivalent norms. The best equivalence constant is therefore a natural quantitative invariant of exactly that construction. The formula is uniform in \(\alpha\ge0\), works for the whole positive-contraction Möbius family, and turns the paper's concrete infinite-dimensional example into the exact value \(\sqrt7\). This quantifies how far the nonrigid example is from an isometric coincidence and can be used when transporting operator estimates between the two norms. It is not an arbitrary finite slice or a table recomputation.
